My thinking:

I been doing wheat and maize same way for many years. My mother-in-law teached me, and I watch what Wang family next field does — they get good harvest so I copy. I don't read the bags much, I just know how many to buy.

For my 10.1 mu, I do wheat in winter, maize in summer, like everyone here.

**Wheat (winter one):**
I plant in October after the maize come off. I use the good seed from the dealer in town — he sells the same one to everybody, Jimai kind I think. Not the old seed my grandmother used. The new ones give more.

For fertilizer, I buy the compound bag — the one with three numbers, 15-15-15. I put about 2 bags per mu before planting. That's 100 jin, 50 kg. Then when wheat turn green in spring I put urea, maybe 25-30 jin per mu. If the wheat look yellow I put more. Better put too much than let it go yellow — one bad wheat year and we eat less all winter.

Water — I pump from the well. Winter water before frost, then green-up water, then when head come out, then when grain filling. 4 times. Sometimes 3 if rain come.

Spray — aphids and the rust sickness. Usually 2 times spring.

Last year I got maybe 900 jin per mu, so 450 kg. Good year maybe 500.

**Maize (summer):**
Right after wheat I plant, no time to plough properly, just the rotary machine, I hire the man with tractor. Hybrid seed of course, Zhengdan type, everyone plant that.

Before planting I put compound fertilizer, about 1.5 bag per mu. Then when maize is knee-high I side-dress urea, maybe 30 jin per mu. Big ear time I want dark green leaves.

Water 2 times if the rain not enough — July and August when ear filling.

Spray 2 times — for the borer worm and the mite.

Maize do better than wheat usually, maybe 1100 jin, 550 kg.

I spend maybe 400-500 yuan per mu on fertilizer total for both crops. Can't spend more, we have 6 mouths and my husband work in city only part-time.
